title: Chemical short-range order increases the phonon heat conductivity in a refractory high-entropy alloy

recollection.starting_material: Guess: A refractory high-entropy alloy, likely based on elements such as Nb, Mo, Ta, W, and possibly V
recollection.intervention: Guess: Heat treatments or alloying protocols designed to promote chemical short-range order (SRO) without long-range ordering; possibly annealing at intermediate temperatures followed by quenching
recollection.structure: Guess: Formation of regions with pronounced local chemical ordering within an overall single-phase BCC solid-solution matrix
recollection.mechanism: Guess: SRO reduces mass and force-constant disorder on neighboring sites, leading to diminished phonon scattering and thus higher lattice thermal conductivity
recollection.results: Guess: Lattice thermal conductivity increased by perhaps 30–50 % compared with the fully random solid solution; corroborated by inelastic neutron or X-ray scattering and first-principles or molecular-dynamics simulations

score.note: The recollection generically identifies promotion of SRO but incorrectly proposes heat treatment rather than Monte Carlo-controlled ordering. It describes local order in a BCC matrix but misses the B2-like HfTi/TiZr clusters and percolating pathways. The reduced-disorder/phonon-scattering mechanism is substantially correct, though it omits percolation and phonon-DOS effects. The estimated 30–50% increase is far from the actual ~12%.
